cert.legal_art41: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), Art. 41: an electronic time stamp shall not be denied legal effect solely because it is in electronic form; a qualified electronic time stamp enjoys the presumption of the accuracy of the date and time it indicates and of the integrity of the data to which it is bound, and is recognised in all Member States.
cert.legal_not_qtsp: XVcache is not a qualified trust service provider. The qualified token is issued by Certigna.
cert.legal_not: This certificate is not a report by a judicial officer (bailiff), not a qualified electronic signature and not legal advice. It proves that a fingerprint existed at a date; it proves neither the author nor the content.
cert.legal_hash_only: The content of the document was never transmitted, only its fingerprint.
cert.legal_court: Its concrete evidential weight is assessed by the court under national procedure.
cert.mt_notice: Translation not yet reviewed by a legal professional; the English version prevails.
cert.verdict_intact: Intact — this document is identical to the one timestamped on {date}.
cert.verdict_invalid: This proof cannot be validated: the file, the date or the token no longer match.
cert.verdict_pending: Pending — the qualified timestamp has not been issued yet.

offer.pitch: XVcache gives law firms qualified electronic timestamps under EU law. Under Art. 41 of the eIDAS Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, a qualified timestamp is presumed accurate as to its date and time and as to the integrity of the stamped data, and it is recognised in every Member State. Only the document's SHA-256 fingerprint is sent, never its content. Each result is a verdict (V intact / X modified) and a one-page PDF certificate in 24 EU languages. Limits: not a bailiff report, not a signature, not legal advice; the evidential weight is for the court.

offer.present_body: XVcache proves that a document existed, unchanged, at a given date. Under Art. 41 of the eIDAS Regulation, the qualified timestamp (issued by Certigna) is presumed accurate and is recognised throughout the EU. Only the document's fingerprint is sent, never its content. You receive a verdict (V intact / X modified) and a one-page PDF certificate.
